writeup.key_factor: ALCS Game 3, series tied 1-1. The model makes Tampa Bay a 52.9% favorite (fair +89) with the starting pitchers rated even: Griffin Jax (3.53 ERA, 3.14 as a starter) against Gavin Williams (3.76 ERA). The market is pricing Williams' elite strikeout form (33% K rate, dominant October outings of 11 and 12 strikeouts) as a clear edge — at +115, BetUS implies only 46.5% for Tampa Bay. The model sees a coin-flip pitching matchup and takes the plus price.
writeup.risk: Williams' peripherals are genuinely elite (DRA- 69) — if he is really pitching like an ace right now (+45 tier instead of the +20 used here), Tampa Bay's win probability falls to about 51% and the edge shrinks toward +3%. Jax also works short outings (~4 innings), so Tampa Bay's bullpen carries more of this game than Cleveland's.

writeup.key_factor: Our model makes Buffalo 54% even with captain Rasmus Dahlin confirmed out — the number already discounts him. Toronto is also missing Tanev and Domi, and +103 sits above our -104 minimum.
writeup.risk: Buffalo's penalty kill has struggled early and this is a road back-to-back spot; if Toronto's power play gets rolling early, the price edge can disappear fast.

writeup.key_factor: The underdog gets the points: our model has Denver covering +2.5 about 56% of the time — it wins outright nearly half the time and the +2.5 also cashes a one- or two-point loss. Better vehicle than the moneyline tonight.
writeup.risk: Denver's secondary is banged up (Surtain II and Hufanga out); if Seattle's passing game exploits it early and Denver has to chase, the cushion can vanish.
